question: GQ-004
subject: re-verifying the 81 after the Gutenberg exclusion changed the list
why: My fetchability sample was 6 items taken BEFORE the mirror rule removed 25. A sample of a list that has since changed is not a sample of the current list.

fetchability.verdict: All institutional. Every sampled item is fetchable and none is a user upload.

the_new_finding.observation: Every sampled identifier came from a MEDICAL heritage library — Royal College of Physicians, Glasgow, Wellcome, RCP Edinburgh.
essays_titles: The London magazine, or, Gentleman's monthly intelligencer. 1748.
the_new_finding.reading: The Essays tier is medical-library SERIALS, not essays in the Library's sense. IA's subject tagging is far looser than the catalogue I derived the subjects from — "Essays" on IA includes 18th century medical periodicals.

English poetry: John Donne, his flight from mediaevalism
but_not_all_tiers.reading: Poetry and cookery are ON SUBJECT. Only Essays drifted. The method works; one subject term is too loose on IA.

what_this_means: Subject names do not transfer between catalogues. I matched "Essays" against the Library's book_subject and assumed IA meant the same thing. For poetry and cookery it does; for essays it does not. Any future source needs this checked per subject rather than assumed for the set.
recommendation: Drop the Essays tier (30 of 81) or re-scope it. That leaves ~51 candidates that are genuinely on-subject, institutional, and fetchable.
